title: Blended operations and autodial
blurb: How agents move between inbound, autodial, and outbound without lying to the dialer.
summary: Blended is a staffing plan. Autodial is the scripted outbound. Predictive people should stay dedicated.

lessons.title: Blended is a staffing plan
objectives: Define blended from the product page
paragraphs: The outbound product page says outbound works with inbound digital channels and that blended behavior lets agents move between inbound and outbound as inbound rises and falls. It does not add a campaign type named Blended to the planning roadmap.

You blend by which skills an agent holds and which campaigns are running, not by a secret fourth object. If inbound and a predictive book share the same people, the dialer is predicting availability it does not have.
uncertain: A community test note says predictive agents should not also be skilled for inbound. That is consistent with the product story and is still a field note, not a settings screenshot.

lessons.title: Autodial is the IVR's outbound
paragraphs: Autodial is the third campaign type. The planning topic groups it with inbound when it tells you to record prompts and build IVR scripts. It still uses lists, like outbound. Think of it as the dialer reaching a person and then handing them a script, not an agent, unless the script transfers.
Skill assignment for autodial uses the same oddly named tab as inbound: Outbound Skills. An autodial campaign that is not running will not place those calls.

lessons.title: Priority and ratio are campaign settings
paragraphs: The campaign admin tree includes a topic for campaign priority and ratio settings. This lab has not quoted that topic's fields, so it will not invent the numbers. What is safe to say is that inbound priority, Skill Transfer priority, and any campaign ratio are different screens until you have read them.
A blend fails when every campaign is 'the important one.' Write the order down: which campaign may steal an agent, and which may not.

lessons.title: Not Ready is a real state
objectives: Subtract Not Ready before you pace
paragraphs: Agents are not always available. TCPA manual touch forces Not Ready when preview time runs out, and it does not dial. A blend that assumes every login is a dialer resource will over-predict.
Reason codes and Not Ready are how you explain the gap. They are not a carrier outage. Reports in the agent category are where you see the pattern before you add lines.

lessons.title: After-call work feeds the next dial
objectives: Let dispositions decide the next dial
paragraphs: A disposition is what the dialer remembers. A final code stops the record. A retryable code brings it back after the redial rules. Wrap time, in the simulator, is the gap before the agent is free again. Five9's pause-before-transfer is a different gap, on the next inbound delivery, and it is not reported as hold.
If wrap is fiction and pause is zero, a blended agent finishes one call and is instantly eligible. That is how a progressive book and an inbound queue trade the same person every few seconds.

lessons.title: Digital and voice share the person
paragraphs: The outbound page says the dialer works with inbound digital engagement, and Agent Desktop Plus is the screen where voice, digital, and context are meant to meet. A blend that is only a voice story misses chat and email sitting on the same login.
Antivirus products can block digital text from loading. The technical requirements name that failure. A 'blend' that cannot show the chat is a desktop failure, not a skill failure.

lessons.title: A blend you can defend
objectives: Defend a blend with six screens
Keep the simulator in the classroom
paragraphs: A defensible blend is a paragraph: which campaigns run, which skills overlap, which mode each outbound book uses, who may be stolen, what Not Ready does to the count, and which abandon window the domain uses. Every noun in that paragraph is a screen you can open.
If you cannot point at the screen, it is not a design. The simulator can illustrate it. It cannot be attached to the domain.

steps.title: Ready
